item.title: Kiah Stokes limits Angel Reese, lights up from 3 to lead Valkyries past Dream in Game 5
item.description: Golden State Valkyries center Kiah Stokes (41) knocks the ball away from Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese (5) during the first half of the WNBA Finals Game 5 at Chase Center in San Francisco, Monday, Oct. 26, 2026. (Carlos Avila Gonzalez/S.F. Chronicle) The Golden State Valkyries and Atlanta Dream are going where no WNBA team has gone before: Deep into a best-of-seven series. These teams have faced off, learned tendencies and flown back-and-forth to each other's cities for weeks. Stripped of most unknowns on Monday in Game 5, both teams played to their strength: Defense. The resulting slugfest produced one of the lowest-scoring Finals games in WNBA history. It also put the Valkyries one win from a championship. Golden State's 64-55 win at Chase Center gave it a 3-2 series lead with Game 6 on Thursday at 9:30 a.m. PT in Atlanta. Center Kiah Stokes was the center of it all, making her case for MVP of these Finals. The Valkyries knew they'd go as far as their defense would take them. While that started with Gabby Williams and Veronica Burton fortifying the point of attack, Stokes has been breaking down opposing teams' stars and breaking records as an elite rim protector. In the Valkyries' wins, Stokes has been the key to limiting Angel Reese as her primary defender. As Game 5 turned into a muddy defensive battle, Stokes prevented Reese from penetrating to the paint, shutting down any glimmer of the Angel Show that starred in the Dream's victories in Games 2 and 3. Reese scored seven points, shooting 2-for-8 from the field, and wrangled 15 rebounds, unable to get a double-double for a second straight game. Stokes tallied three blocks for a sixth straight game, tying with Lisa Leslie in 2003 for the longest such streak in a single postseason in WNBA playoff history. In Game 4, she set the WNBA record for total blocks in a Finals series with 14. She and Veronica Burton led the Valkyries' rebounding frenzy with eight apiece. Unlike the rest of her playoffs, Stokes was a primary scorer and got relatively hot from deep, making 3 of 4 from beyond the arc. Her three 3-pointers are her playoff career high over her nine career trips to the postseason. Her 13 points tied her season high and matched Burton for a team high Monday. item.title: Valkyries could be forced to celebrate championship on practice court
item.description: Gabby Williams of the Golden State Valkyries signs autographs as she leaves the court following her team's victory against the Atlanta Dream in Game 4 of the 2026 WNBA Finals at State Farm Arena on Oct. 24, 2026 in Atlanta. (Kevin C. Cox/Getty Images) The Golden State Valkyries might end up in the awkward position of having to celebrate a historic championship win at an auxiliary gym. The Valkyries secured a 3-2 series lead against the Dream on Monday, beating Atlanta 64-55 at home to bring Golden State one win away from winning a championship just two seasons into its existence. However, if they pull off the win on Thursday, the celebrations might not take place in the traditional setting of the court the winning team secured victory on. They could be at a practice court instead. This is according to ESPN's Ramona Shelburne, who was on Monday's NBA Today to discuss the ongoing scheduling mess that the WNBA faces for the Finals . While the Atlanta will continue to host every Finals matchup at State Farm Arena, an over-17,000-seat arena where the Atlanta Hawks play, the trade-off is that they'll have to play Game 6 at 12:30 p.m. locally (that's 9:30 a.m. for those in California) and will have to quickly move out of the arena for the full-time NBA tenants before their scheduled 8 p.m. local tip-off. This scheduling crunch has already happened with Game 4, where teams and media were basically rushed out the door after the postgame interviews finished. This was done to avoid hosting a Finals game at the Dream's normal home: the 3,500-seat Gateway Center Arena in College Park. As a result, any possible Valkyries celebrations will have to wait. "That championship celebration may not actually be on that court," Shelburne said on a television appearance . "I've heard there are discussions about whether there's enough time to turn the arena over in time for the fans to celebrate on the court. It could be moved to like a practice court... Look, 12:30, you just do the math. "And what do you want to do, tell people to wrap up your celebrations so we can get the Hawks game started?" Shelburne added. "It's not a great option, but it's the option they've chosen." A championship was always going to mean making history for Golden State. But, in potentially hoisting a championship trophy at a practice court, it seems like there will be some history that might not be as worth celebrating. item.title: Heat blow 4th-quarter lead to Mavericks, fall to 0-4 despite Giannis Antetokounmpo triple-double
item.description: Giannis Antetokounmpo continues to fill up the box score. But it's not translating to wins for the Miami Heat. On the heels of three straight losses to start the season, the Heat held a 90-84 lead early in the fourth at home against the Dallas Mavericks Monday night. But Cooper Flagg took over down the stretch with 12 of his 29 points in the final stanza to lead the Mavericks to a 113-109 win. Flagg added 11 assists, 5 steals and 3 blocks and looks just fine after missing a game with a shoulder strain . Giannis triple-double, but no win The loss for Miami spoiled another big effort from Antetokounmpo, who tallied 29 points, 14 rebounds and 11 assists for his first triple-double since joining Miami from the Milwaukee Bucks. It also dropped the Heat to 0-4, in a desperate search for the first win of the season. Three of those losses have come at home, and the buzz of the Giannis era has quickly given way to anxiety in Miami. Giannis Antetokounmpo and the Heat remain in search of their first win together. IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect / REUTERS What's wrong with the Heat? The loss continues a trend for the Giannis Heat, who have gotten big efforts from the former MVP in each of his four starts. Antetokounmpo entered Monday averaging 28.3 points, 8 rebounds, 3 assists and 1.3 steals through his first three games. But those games resulted in double-digit losses at home to the Timberwolves and Pistons and a 115-110 road loss to the Hornets on Saturday. The season-opening national TV showcase against the Wolves quickly turned into a 131-106 laugher in Minnesota's favor. The shutdown defense that was expected from the frontline tandem of Antetokounmpo and Bam Adebayo has yet to materialize as the Heat have surrendered 113-plus points in each of their four games. And the Heat are struggling to find a reliable second option on offense behind a ball-dominant Antetokounmpo. Davion Mitchell so far looks like it. He entered Monday averaging 17 points and posted 21 against the Mavericks. But it wasn't enough to secure the win. The Heat are also struggling to control the boards and have lost the rebounding margin in each of their four games. With the Mavericks' 51-42 edge Monday night, the Heat have a 202-152 rebounding deficit through four games. It's early, of course, but this surely isn't how the Heat envisioned the start of their new era after the high-profile offseason deal to acquire Antetokounmpo. Their next chances to get into the win column come on the road on Wednesday against the Hawks and at home on Friday against the Pacers. From there, they'll embark on a five-game West Coast swing with games against the Lakers, Clippers, Warriors, Kings and Jazz. Starting a trip like that without a win does not sound like a good time.

item.title: Why Tarik Skubal ‘doesn’t buy’ Dodgers’ World Series window is closed
item.description: Jayne Kamin-Oncea-Imagn Images Why Tarik Skubal ‘doesn’t buy’ Dodgers’ World Series window is closed appeared first on ClutchPoints . Add ClutchPoints as a Preferred Source by clicking here . The Milwaukee Brewers are on the cusp of winning the World Series . No matter who wins this year’s Fall Classic, they will be the first new World Series champion since 2023. The Los Angeles Dodgers won it all in 2024 and 2025. Los Angeles wanted to do so again in 2026. They traded for Tarik Skubal , a pending free agent, in an effort to bolster their pitching staff for the run ahead. Los Angeles fell in the NLCS to the Brewers. But Skubal isn’t a fan of people saying that the Dodgers’ window is closed. “I don’t feel that at all. It’s hard to win the World Series and this group has done it the last two seasons. I think this group is incredibly talented,” Skubal said, via Dodgers Nation and Maddie Lee of the LA Times. Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial) Skubal split the 2026 season between the Detroit Tigers and the Dodgers. He had some brilliant moments with Los Angeles following his early August trade out West. He finished the regular season with a 12-7 record and a 2.76 ERA. The Dodgers made the NLCS for the third straight season. As mentioned, though, they were defeated by the Brewers. More than that, the series wasn’t much of a contest. Milwaukee swept the Dodgers in four games to reach the World Series. It’s not a question of talent for Los Angeles. This team certainly has the talent to make another run at it. They just need to put it all together again in 2027. Whether Skubal will be there for the Dodgers’ next attempt at the World Series remains to be seen.

item.title: Rangers bring road game back home among takeaways from 6-3 loss to Kings
item.description: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect If you didn’t know any better, you would’ve thought the New York Rangers were playing on the road Monday night, and not at Madison Square Garden. It’s not just that the Rangers lost their first game at home this season, but more so the manner with which they dropped a 6-3 decision to the Los Angeles Kings. Slow start. Early goals against. Chasing the game. Largely uninspired and unstructured play defensively. Subpar goaltending. Not nearly enough offensive chances nor zone time. You name it, and the Rangers (7-6-1) were pretty much deficient in that facet of the game. That this mess happened on home ice stands out because the Rangers were not only a perfect 6-0-0 at MSG this season, scoring first in all six games, but they hadn’t trailed for a single second of the 360 minutes played previously in their building. Of course, that was impossible to keep up over a 42-game home schedule. But the fact that the Rangers brought all the bad elements from their poor road play back home with them after a winless trek to Canada late last week was at least a bit unexpected. With 38-year-old James Reimer making his Rangers debut between the pipes, neither he nor his teammates were up to the Kings fast start Monday. A neutral zone breakdown in the middle of the ice led to Taylor Ward breaking in all alone to beat Reimer between the pads on the first shot of the game just 1:15 into the first period. The Kings then made it 2-0 at 4:52, when Joel Armia’s cross-crease pass was buried by Brandt Clarke during a 6-on-5 with an extended delayed penalty. Los Angeles goal! Scored by Brandt Clarke with 15:08 left in the 1st. Assisted by Scott Laughton and Joel Armia. Miller had a Tye Kartye pass go in off this skates at 13:01 on New York’s second recorded shot of the period, but Drew Doughty answered right back for L.A. at 17:32, sending a long shot past Reimer to make it 3-1. Coach Mike Sullivan pulled Reimer after the first period, and Dylan Garand promptly gave up a power-play goal to former Rangers star Artemi Panarin at 1:30 of the second, and Mikey Anderson drove a long slap shot through his pads at 6:54. The Rangers actually caught a break 32 seconds later when Clarke pushed the puck over the goal line to seemingly make it 6-1. Sullivan’s coach’s challenge proved successful when it was ruled that Clarke shoved Garand’s glove with his stick to send the puck in, making for goalie interference. The rest was the rest, the Rangers got to within 5-3 at 16:08 of the third period, but an empty-net goal 29 seconds later iced the win for the Kings. If some or all of this sounds similar to New York’s 7-4 road loss to the Ottawa Senators on Saturday and the 5-4 road defeat in Toronto against the Maple Leafs on Thursday, well that’s because it was eerily similar. item.description: Changes are being made this week, and Dan Lanning isn't shying away from them. The Oregon Ducks are still reeling from yet another ugly offensive performance in a 21-10 road loss to Illinois. That turned out to be the final straw for offensive coordinator Drew Mehringer , who was fired on Sunday after three straight games with less than 20 points.
